implementations.cpp_cuda: independent LibTorch C++ control layer with ATen CUDA kernels
implementations.fsl_cpu: official FSL FLIRT CPU C++ executable

coordinate_contract.fsl_flirt_matrix: input-to-reference transform in FSL scaled-mm coordinates
coordinate_contract.package_affine: moving-to-fixed world-RAS transform; inverse fixed-to-moving world-RAS pull is used for sampling
coordinate_contract.synthmorph_sampling: fixed-grid fixed-to-moving target-to-source pull, exported as physical RAS displacement
coordinate_contract.comparison_rule: compare warped volumes on a common grid, or convert direction and coordinate basis before comparing transforms

interpretation.matched_backend_conclusion: The C++ CUDA control path was 1.49 times as fast as Python/PyTorch for hot matched compute and saved 0.6373 seconds per subject.
interpretation.package_decision: Keep Python/PyTorch as the package backend because the measured absolute saving does not justify compiler, PyTorch ABI, and platform-specific wheel maintenance.
interpretation.fsl_boundary: FSL FLIRT uses a different optimizer and search procedure; its timing and output differences cannot be attributed solely to language or CPU/GPU backend.
interpretation.load_boundary: Severe shared-node contention was observed. All timing values are descriptive for these runs, not clean hardware throughput estimates.

privacy: Aggregate-only; source paths, subject identifiers, PIDs, and per-case values are excluded.
